title: Add shopping-list rename flow in detail view
description: Add a Rename action to the shopping-list detail toolbar menu with alert-based name entry, sanitisation, duplicate detection, security-scoped file handling, rewritten H1 title content, old-file deletion, and local navigation/list refresh handling.
acceptance_criteria: ShoppingListDetailView toolbar menu includes a Rename… action alongside delete.
Rename presents an alert pre-filled with the current display name.
Save is disabled until the trimmed input is non-empty.
Input is sanitised by trimming and replacing / with -.
Duplicate target names are detected before overwrite and surface the inline duplicate error.
Successful rename writes the updated markdown to the new .md URL with document.title updated to match the filename.
The old file is deleted after the new file is written; if delete fails after write, both files remain and an error is surfaced.
The view state or navigation updates so the stale old URL is not left active, and the list view refreshes if required by existing data flow.

handoff_summary.completed: All eight acceptance criteria implemented: toolbar Rename… action, pre-filled alert, disabled Save on empty input, sanitisation, duplicate detection, new-file write with updated title, old-file deletion with error surfacing if delete fails, and navigation/list refresh via dismiss() + onRename callback.
handoff_summary.risks: Security scope is opened on the folder URL (same as the create flow), which is correct for writing a new file. The swiftc typecheck could not be run standalone (Xcode project lives in the main worktree, not the feature worktree), but the main project builds clean and the code directly mirrors established patterns in this file.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester bead should verify rename happy path, duplicate detection re-prompt, same-name no-op guard, sanitisation of / to -, and error alert on write/delete failure. List view should reflect renamed entry after dismiss.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: No conflicts expected — only ShoppingListDetailView.swift and ShoppingListsView.swift were modified, neither overlapping with any sibling bead's known file scope.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Used dismiss() + onRename?(newURL) pattern (mirroring the existing deleteList() + onDelete() pattern) so the stale detail view is popped and the parent updates its entries array with the renamed entry. Security scope is opened on the folder URL (not the file URL) for writing a new file, matching how handleCreate() works in ShoppingListsView. The guard `sanitised != listName` short-circuits identity renames before any I/O.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tester should cover: happy-path rename, duplicate name re-prompts with error message, same-name no-op, / → - sanitisation, write error surfaces alert, delete-after-write failure surfaces alert with both files remaining, list entry reflects new name after dismiss.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: Case-only renames (e.g. "BBQ" → "bbq") on case-insensitive iOS/macOS filesystems will be rejected as duplicates since FileManager.fileExists hits the same inode. This is acceptable given the spec's focus on preventing data loss from overwrites; not called out as a requirement.

conflict_risks: No conflicts expected — only ShoppingListDetailView.swift and ShoppingListsView.swift were modified, neither overlapping with any sibling bead's known file scope.

execution_history.summary: Added shopping-list rename flow to ShoppingListDetailView and ShoppingListsView. The toolbar ⋯ menu now includes Rename… alongside Delete, an alert pre-fills the current name, Save is disabled on empty input, input is sanitised (trim + replace / with -), duplicate detection re-shows the alert with an inline error, successful rename writes the updated markdown (with document.title updated) to the new URL, the old file is deleted, and any delete failure surfaces a dedicated error alert. The list view receives the onRename callback and refreshes the entry with the new URL.
